A pressure cooker doesn't add more heat. Its sealed lid traps steam, pressure rises to about twice normal air pressure, and water then boils at about 120 °C instead of 100 °C. Hotter water cooks food in roughly a third of the time.

2026-11-19_soap-bubbles.mp4.ig:
Why soap bubbles are round

A bubble is a thin skin of soapy water around trapped air, and surface tension makes that skin shrink to the least area. For a fixed volume of air, that shape is a sphere, whatever the wand looks like. Soap makes the skin weaker in tension but self-healing, and its thickness paints the colours.

2026-11-19_projection-matrix.mp4.ig:
Projection matrices: why P squared equals P

Project b = (3, 1) onto the line through (1, 1): P = a aᵀ / aᵀa = ½ [1 1; 1 1], so Pb = (2, 2) and the error (1, −1) is perpendicular to the line. Projecting again changes nothing, so P² = P, and the eigenvalues can only be 0 or 1.

How a hydraulic jack lifts a car

How does a tiny push lift a whole car? A hydraulic jack traps oil between a small piston and a big one, and Pascal's law does the rest: 50 newtons in, 5,000 newtons out. The catch? You push 100 times farther.

Why (AB) transpose reverses the order
